modalLead: A Notes widget, page templates to share, quiet hours for alerts and a Trend tab in Collection health.

items.text: A Notes widget. Write in Markdown, tick checkboxes on the tile, type / for commands such as the date or a table, and open it large with a preview. New installs start with an example.
Retry on a stopped feed. A feed that gave up has a Retry button in the Feeds widget.
Share a page as a template file. Your own addresses become names the importer fills in; nothing about usage or health goes in the file. Import one from the page menu or start an empty page from it.
Quiet hours. Alerts that arrive at night are held, and one summary tells you in the morning what is still down and what recovered.
Reminders for an outage that goes on, every so often and not more than you choose.
Collection health has a Trend tab and more figures: key numbers, what to fix first, when links were last checked and how often they are opened, and uptime by weekday.
Uptime badges for a README or a post, off until you switch them on.
Background re-checks are on by default, so Health stays current without a dashboard open.
Search finds links waiting in the inbox, and the Inbox icon says how many are kept.
The Bookmarks view shows containers. A bookmark that is a container's web UI gets a cube after its name — green running, amber paused, grey stopped — and a click opens that container.
Config lists the small cards in the corner, with Show again, and one of them points at the feature overview on nextdash.cc.
The selection bar on the dashboard can fetch icons and previews, the same buttons the Bookmarks view already had.
A daily install count. Once a day nextDash sends a random id and its version number so the project can count installs — nothing else. On by default; switch it off under Behavior → Privacy & sync.
